title: Maximum Subset XOR
description: Given an array `nums` of non-negative integers, choose any subset of elements (possibly empty, whose XOR is `0`) so that the bitwise XOR of all chosen elements is as large as possible. Return this maximum subset XOR value.
hints: Think of each integer as a 31-bit vector over GF(2) and maintain a linear XOR basis where `basis[b]` holds a basis vector whose highest set bit is `b`.
After building the basis by reducing each number against existing basis vectors, greedily XOR `ans` with `basis[b]` from the highest bit down whenever `ans ^ basis[b] > ans`.

examples.explanation: Choosing {2, 5} yields 2 ^ 5 = 7, the maximum possible subset XOR.
All elements are 0, so the maximum subset XOR is 0.
